questions.stem: Management asks a safety professional to omit an imminent life-safety hazard from a report. What is the most ethical response?
options: Remove it to protect the client relationship
Delay reporting until an injury occurs
Describe it only as a minor housekeeping issue
Report the hazard objectively and advise appropriate parties of the unacceptable risk
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: The BCSP Code requires holding safety and health paramount and advising employers, clients, employees, the public, and authorities of danger and unacceptable risk.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Professional judgment should not be compromised to conceal serious risk.
Waiting for harm violates preventive responsibility.
Mischaracterizing the hazard is deceptive and can prevent protection.
questions.sourceLocation: BCSP Code of Ethics, Standard 1; Yates Chapter 40

questions.stem: A client requests a specialized radiation-shielding design outside the professional current competence. What should the professional do?
options: Disclose the limitation and obtain or refer to qualified expertise
Accept the work and learn after issuing the design
Use an unrelated past project without review
Hide the lack of experience from the client
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Ethical practice requires assignments to be undertaken only when qualified and qualifications to be represented accurately.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Learning is valuable, but safety-critical work requires competent supervision before professional conclusions are issued.
An unrelated design may not fit the source, energy, geometry, or regulatory basis.
Concealment misrepresents qualifications and exposes people to risk.
questions.sourceLocation: BCSP Code of Ethics, Standards 4 and 5; Yates Chapter 40

questions.stem: A consultant receives an undisclosed commission if a specific vendor product is selected. What is required?
options: Keep it confidential because the product may be good
Disclose and manage the conflict so professional judgment remains independent
Recommend the product without evaluating alternatives
Transfer the commission to a family member
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Professional relations should be conducted with integrity and conflicts that could compromise judgment must be avoided or transparently managed.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Potential product quality does not remove the conflict or disclosure duty.
A recommendation must be based on objective needs and evidence.
Changing the recipient does not eliminate the conflict.
questions.sourceLocation: BCSP Code of Ethics, Standard 6; Yates Chapter 40

questions.stem: A company asks the safety professional to state publicly that a control is proven effective when verification data are incomplete. What is the ethical response?
options: Make the claim because management approved it
Present an estimate as measured fact
State only what the available facts support and disclose the uncertainty
Omit all limitations to avoid confusion
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Public statements should be objective, truthful, and founded on facts and competence.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Management approval does not convert an unsupported statement into fact.
Material limitations are needed for objective interpretation.
questions.sourceLocation: BCSP Code of Ethics, Standards 2 and 3; Yates Chapter 40

questions.stem: A candidate has passed a course but has not earned the CSP credential. How should the qualification be represented?
options: Use CSP because the exam is planned
Use the credential if a supervisor approves
Add CSP with a small disclaimer hidden elsewhere
Describe the course accurately and do not claim the CSP credential
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Academic and professional qualifications and levels of responsibility must be represented accurately.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Future intent does not confer a credential.
An employer cannot grant a BCSP certification.
A hidden disclaimer does not correct a misleading credential claim.
questions.sourceLocation: BCSP Code of Ethics, Standard 5; Yates Chapter 40

questions.stem: A credential holder discovers credible evidence that another credential holder falsified exposure data. What is the ethical course?
options: Preserve the evidence, use appropriate reporting channels, and notify BCSP when warranted
Ignore the evidence because reporting another professional could damage the profession reputation
Post the allegation publicly before its authenticity, context, and reporting obligations are evaluated
Correct the exposure records quietly without preserving the original data or documenting the concern
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: The code calls for integrity, truthful records, and action to bring professional misconduct by another status holder to BCSP attention.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Concealing serious misconduct undermines public protection and professional integrity.
Public accusation without due process can be unfair and unsupported.
Silent alteration destroys traceability and does not address misconduct.
questions.sourceLocation: BCSP Code of Ethics, Standards 2 and 6; BCSP policies and forms
